children: Stocks are firmly in the red on Tuesday, as investors fret over a combination of negative catalysts, including oil nearing $100 a barrel again, as attacks around the Gulf intensify, and the Japanese yen on a tear.

The rally in the yen threatens to plunge previously lucrative carry trades under water - something that hit global equities in August 2024, when a sudden strengthening in the Japanese currency unleashed a storm of volatility.
Copper is in the spotlight, as the possibility of U.S. tariffs continues to suck metal from the global market into U.S. warehouses. LME copper futures
are up 0.8% at $14,627 a ton, around record highs, which is offering a cushion to the FTSE
, which is only down 0.3% compared with the 0.5% drop in the DAX
is down 0.4% on the day. A 10% drop in shares of Novartis following a second unsuccessful drug trial, is combining with declines in other heavyweights such as HSBC
, down 0.6%, to offset gains of 1.1% to 1.5% in Shell
